assertions.name: G_in_planck_units_is_identically_one
assertions.source: G_q*(hbar_q/c_q)^2 = 1 as a rational function of q, matching g-q-closed-form.md — the corpus's q-forms are mutually consistent

assertions.name: t_P_dimensional_closed_form
assertions.source: sqrt(hbar_q G_q / c_q^5) = sqrt(q)*|q-1| exactly. The Abs survives because `q` is declared positive but not >1; on the framework's own domain q0 > 1 it reads sqrt(q)*(q-1). Stated with the Abs rather than assuming the domain into the identity

assertions.name: planck_triple_is_free_of_calibration
assertions.source: each of ell_P, m_P, t_P is a function of q ALONE — no m_e, no CODATA, no SI G, so none of them is a calibration

assertions.name: three_planck_lengths_are_pairwise_distinct
assertions.source: the normalised total, the per-step share and the dimensional form are three inequivalent expressions carrying one name

assertions.name: share_and_dimensional_differ_by_more_than_ten_at_q0
assertions.source: at the proton q0 they differ by a factor 10.6332

data.corrects: This session's own audit §5, which framed the Planck length as forbidden / a fourth calibration. Owner correction: it is not a calibration, it is written symbolically in q. What the corpus forbids is pinning the SUBSTRATE at m_Planck (importing SI G as an input fixing q0), which is a different move.
data.scope: Derives and compares; settles no physics. Does not claim the dimensional sqrt(q) is the 'right' Planck length nor that either corpus form is wrong — only that three inequivalent expressions carry one name, and that none is a calibration. Which one a given block MEANS is an author question.

q0AnchorReason: the numeric column is evaluated at the standing proton default; the algebra is anchor-free
